channel.title: Western New York Catholic - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Western New York Catholic (wnycatholic.org)

item.title: Abuse victims agree to $246 million from Diocese of Rochester
item.description: Hundreds of clergy abuse victims agreed to a massive settlement from the Diocese of Rochester this week, bringing the diocese’s yearslong bankruptcy proceedings closer to an end.

item.title: Conference offers tips on strengthening and rebuilding parishes
item.description: A parish community just outside of Baltimore held a conference to show how they rebuilt their parish.

item.title: Legion of Mary to hold weekly rosary at Cheektowaga church
item.description: The Legion of Mary is sponsoring an outdoor public rosary every Monday evening at 6 p.m. in front of Infant of Prague Church at 921 Cleveland Drive, Cheektowaga.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV announces dates for World Youth Day in South Korea
item.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday announced that the dates of the next World Youth Day, to be held in Seoul, South Korea, will be Aug. 3-8, 2027.

item.title: SS. Peter & Paul opens its doors to homeschool students in grades 1-8
item.description: SS. Peter & Paul School, a pillar of classical education in Williamsville, is excited to announce new flexible learning options designed specifically for homeschool students in grades 1-8.

item.title: The power of pilgrimage: The National Shrine of the Divine Mercy
item.description: Recently, I and some fellow parishioners participated in a pilgrimage to the National Shrine of the Divine Mercy in Stockbridge, Massachusetts.

item.title: Sisters of St. Francis elect new leadership team
item.description: The Sisters of St. Francis of the Neumann Communities announced the election of a new leadership team.

item.title: Sister Roberta Fulton receives award from Knights of Peter Claver
item.description: Sister Roberta Fulton, SSMN, director of Cultural Diversity and Social Justice for the Diocese of Buffalo, received the Grand Lady Award during the national Knights of Peter Claver convention in July.

item.title: We can never say, ‘We knew nothing about that’
item.description: During World War II, historical accounts vary as to how much German citizens knew about Nazi subhuman prisoner work and extermination camps.

item.title: WNYCatholic Newspaper Closes Its Final Chapter
item.description: After more than 150 years of service, the Western New York Catholic—the official newspaper of the Diocese of Buffalo—will come to an end with the recent reductions of personnel at the Catholic Center and Communications Office.
